description: Rock-paper-scissors against the Aero Hand using the camera. Jake shows his throw to the webcam (MediaPipe, reuse teleop.py's tracking) and the hand throws rock, paper or scissors on the count of three. NO cheating: the hand's choice is picked at random (secrets/random) and committed BEFORE Jake's throw is read, never as a reaction to it; log the committed pick first so it can be checked. Announce who won and keep score. Hand moves stay under the 50% speed cap (scripts/hand_speed.py). Add it as a button in the Helping Hands Mac app (voice-7fc650e9) and a helpinghands://aero URL.

results.identified_issue: Relaxed pose is a hand-picked JOINTS['relaxed'] = thumb [30,15,20], fingers 30 deg each (not tuned on hardware). Shoot speed: hand_speed.limit(hand, max(SHOOT_PCT=60, base)) right before the shoot set_joint_positions, restored to base after the 0.8 s READ_S window so the servos aren't slowed mid-travel; max() keeps the Full speed toggle (AERO_SPEED_PCT) from being lowered. limit() writes 7 set_speed frames each time, adding a little latency at shoot. hand_speed import moved to module top so dry-run has base_pct. Commit-before-read order unchanged: commit() runs before the count. Not run on the real hand/camera; py_compile only.
results.summary: The countdown now says 3, 2, 1, shoot. The hand sits relaxed and half open on each count, and only the shoot move runs at 60% speed.
results.detailed_description: I changed the countdown in rps.py. The voice now says 3, 2, 1, shoot instead of rock, paper, scissors, and the hand no longer starts from a fist. On each count it goes to a relaxed, half-open hand: thumb partly in, every finger bent about 30 degrees. I picked those angles myself, so tell me if the pose looks wrong. Since it's the same pose every time, the hand moves into it on 3 and then holds still through 2 and 1. On shoot, the speed goes up to 60% just for the move to its committed pick. It drops back to 50% once your throw has been read (0.8 s), so the move isn't slowed partway. Everything else, including the moves back to relaxed, stays at 50%. If the Full speed toggle is on, shoot never goes slower than that setting. The no-cheat order is the same: the hand's pick is chosen with secrets and logged with its hash before the count starts, and before your throw is read. Not tested on the real hand or camera. I only checked that the script compiles.
results.user_reply_draft: Done! The hand now counts 3, 2, 1, shoot. It waits relaxed and half open, then snaps to its throw a little faster on shoot. It still picks its throw at random and writes it down before it looks at yours.

results.notes: Jake: change the rock-paper-scissors countdown. Don't cycle through rock, paper, scissors while counting. Count '3, 2, 1, shoot' (or say 'rock, paper, scissors, shoot'), and on each count the hand goes to a partially open, relaxed hand. On 'shoot' it moves to its committed random pick at 60% speed. That is Jake's explicit exception to the 50% cap and applies only to the shoot move; everything else stays at 50%. Keep the no-cheat rule (pick committed and logged before reading his throw).

results.identified_issue: Classifier is a threshold on teleop.raw_joints pip+dip sums (straight ~0.27, curled ~3.1 per VALLEY_PEAK); untested on live webcam. Hand throw is sent via set_joint_positions (speed-capped by firmware SET_SPE) rather than pose.py's run_trajectory glide so the camera loop never blocks. Pose joint lists duplicated from pose.py since pose.py executes at import; if those poses change, update JOINTS in rps.py. Commitment: secrets.choice + token_hex nonce, sha256(throw:nonce) logged to rps_log.jsonl before reading the human throw; reveal printed after.
results.summary: Added rock-paper-scissors: a Games → Rock paper scissors button and helpinghands://aero/rps. The hand's throw is picked with secrets and logged before your throw is read.
results.detailed_description: New script third_party/aero_hand/scripts/rps.py (run via rps.sh, or app.sh rps). It reuses teleop.py's MediaPipe tracking by importing it. Each round goes like this: (1) the hand's throw comes from secrets.choice. Before the count starts it's written with a nonce to ~/HelpingHands-tools/aero/rps_log.jsonl, and its sha256 is printed and shown on the camera preview. (2) The hand makes a fist and macOS 'say' counts rock, paper, scissors, shoot. (3) On shoot the hand moves to its committed throw. Only then is your throw sampled, for 0.8 s, and the most common reading wins. (4) It reveals the throw and nonce so you can check the hash, says who won, and keeps a running score (you / hand / ties). If it can't see your hand, the round doesn't count. Esc or the app's Stop button ends the game, prints the final score and opens the hand. Hand moves go through hand_speed.limit(), so the 50% cap applies unless the Full speed toggle is on. Things to know: your throw is classified with a hardcoded bend threshold (BENT = 1.4 rad of pip+dip bend per finger). I set it from teleop's calibration table, not from your real hand on camera, so it may need tuning. Scissors means index and middle up with ring and pinky down; anything in between reads as no throw. The hand's three poses are copied from pose.py's fist/open/peace, because importing pose.py would run it. Not tested on the real camera or hand. I checked that Python compiles, the classifier gives the right answer on synthetic angles, and the Swift typechecks.
results.user_reply_draft: Rock-paper-scissors is in! Press Games → Rock paper scissors in the Aero Hand window, or open helpinghands://aero/rps. The hand picks its throw at random and writes it down before it looks at yours, so it can't cheat, and it keeps score. If it misreads your throws, tell me and I'll tune it.
